# Discussion Board Business Overview and Objectives

## Overview
This document outlines the business vision, operational objectives, and scope of the Discussion Board platform dedicated to the open exchange of ideas and information on political and economic topics. The platform is designed to foster meaningful dialogues, ensuring a safe, respectful, and high-quality environment for all users, regardless of their background or opinion.

## Vision
The Discussion Board aspires to be the leading digital space where diverse perspectives on political and economic issues converge. By providing a structured, moderated, and user-friendly experience, the platform seeks to cultivate a community that values critical thinking, evidence-based debate, and civil discourse. The end goal is to contribute positively to societal understanding and democratic processes through inclusive conversations.

## Business Objectives
- **Enable Informed Discussions:** Provide reliable tools for users to share knowledge, insights, and opinions on trending political and economic matters.
- **Foster Diversity of Thought:** Encourage respectful participation from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and viewpoints.
- **Ensure Safety and Civility:** Maintain a robust moderation system that addresses abusive behavior, misinformation, and off-topic content while protecting freedom of expression.
- **Drive User Engagement:** Promote active participation through intuitive features—such as voting, commenting, and content sharing—to build a loyal, returning user base.
- **Support Trusted Moderation:** Empower moderators with clear guidelines and efficient tools to manage discussions and upholding the platform’s standards.
- **Continuous Improvement:** Use data-driven insights and feedback loops to refine platform features, moderation policies, and overall user experience.

## Target Audience
- Individuals interested in engaging with political and economic topics
- Professionals, students, and enthusiasts in related fields
- Organizations and communities fostering civil discourse

## Key Features Overview
- Topic-centric discussion threads for both current events and timeless issues
- User authentication and flexible onboarding experiences
- Multi-role system (member, moderator, admin) to enhance operational governance
- Voting, commenting, and content reaction capabilities
- Robust reporting, flagging, and moderation workflows

## Success Metrics
- Growth in user registrations and daily active usage
- High engagement rates (posts, comments, reactions per user)
- Low incidence rates of rule violations and effective moderation response times
- Positive feedback from user satisfaction surveys
- Sustainable retention and expansion of the core user community

## Value Proposition
The Discussion Board delivers a one-stop platform for high-quality conversations on pressing political and economic issues, safeguarding civil exchange and drawing on collective intelligence. By balancing ease of use with principled moderation, the service meets the needs of both casual participants and expert contributors, ensuring every voice can contribute to the evolving public discourse.

# Discussion Board User Roles and Access Control

## 1. Introduction
This document outlines the user roles, permission sets, authentication workflows, and access control logic for the Discussion Board service. Properly delineating these controls ensures a safe, fair, and manageable community space for the exchange of political and economic opinions.

---

## 2. User Roles Overview

| Role        | Description                                                                 |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Member      | General users who can post, comment on, and react to board content.         |
| Moderator   | Users who monitor content, handle reports, and enforce community standards. |
| Admin       | System operators who manage all configurations, policies, and users.        |

<!-- See [03_DiscussionBoard_Main_Features_and_User_Journeys.md](./03_DiscussionBoard_Main_Features_and_User_Journeys.md) for detailed flows by role. -->

---

## 3. Permissions Matrix

| Action                                | Member | Moderator | Admin |
|----------------------------------------|:------:|:---------:|:-----:|
| Register & Authenticate                |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| View Posts & Comments                  |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Create Post/Comment                    |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Edit Own Post/Comment                  |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Delete Own Post/Comment                |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| React (Like/Dislike) to Posts/Comments |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Report Posts/Comments                  |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Moderate (Edit/Delete Any Post/Comment)|        |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Resolve Reports                        |        |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Manage User Roles/Access               |        |           |  ✓   |
| Configure Board Settings/Policy        |        |           |  ✓   |

---

## 4. Access Control & Authentication

- **Registration**: New users register via email or social login; basic verification required.
- **Authentication**: Secure login using username/password or supported OAuth providers.
- **Session Management**: JWT or session cookie used to maintain identity and ensure role-based access enforcement.
- **Role Assignment**: Default role is Member upon registration. Elevated roles (Moderator, Admin) require Admin intervention.
- **Access Validation**: Every sensitive API endpoint enforces authentication and checks role-based permissions per the matrix.

---

## 5. Role Elevation & Demotion Processes
- **Promotion to Moderator/Admin**: Only Admins can elevate users. Such actions must be audited and ideally require secondary authorization, especially for Admin role changes.
- **Demotion/Revocation**: Admin removes elevated rights as needed, based on performance or conduct, with audit trails for accountability.

---

## 6. Security & Compliance Considerations
- Enforce password and session security best practices.
- Rate limit login and critical actions to prevent abuse.
- Log all role changes, moderator actions, and admin activities for traceability.
- Ensure privacy compliance (e.g., GDPR) for user data, especially for role or access logs.

See [05_DiscussionBoard_Service_Overview_and_Architecture.md](./05_DiscussionBoard_Service_Overview_and_Architecture.md) for integrated technical overview.

# Main Features & User Journeys of Discussion Board

This document describes the key features and main user journeys of the Discussion Board, covering member, moderator, and admin roles. It provides an overview of core functionality and integrates essential reference summaries to ensure the page is fully self-contained.

## Table of Contents
1. Overview and Objectives
2. Roles and Access Control
3. Main Features
4. User Journeys
5. Business Rules & Moderation
6. Architecture Overview

---

## 1. Overview and Objectives
The Discussion Board is a digital forum designed to foster transparent and civil dialogue on political and economic topics. Its primary objectives are:
- Enable open discussion, knowledge-sharing, and constructive debate among authenticated users.
- Maintain a secure, moderated environment free from abusive content.
- Ensure role-based access to sensitive features and administrative controls.

## 2. Roles and Access Control
Three principal user roles define access and permissions:
- **Member**: Can create posts, comment, and participate in voting (like/dislike).
- **Moderator**: Monitors discussions, resolves disputes, manages reported content, and can edit or remove posts/comments.
- **Admin**: Configures system settings, manages users and roles, sets discussion policies, and oversees high-level moderation procedures.

## 3. Main Features
- Topic boards for political and economic discussions
- Post creation, editing, reporting, and deletion
- Nested commenting with threading support
- Like/Dislike voting on posts and comments
- Reporting mechanism for inappropriate content
- Moderation tools (approve, hide, edit, delete, manage reports)
- Role-based dashboards (tailored for members, moderators, admins)
- Notification system for mentions, replies, and moderation actions
- Search and filter by topic, user, or date

## 4. User Journeys
### Member
- Discover a topic board, create a post, or respond to an existing post
- Participate in comment threads, like/dislike contributions, and report inappropriate content
- Receive feedback via notifications on activity involving them

### Moderator
- Receive alerts for new reports
- Audit flagged posts/comments, using moderation tools to act (warn, edit, remove, escalate)
- Maintain civil discussion per community guidelines

### Admin
- Set up new boards, configure categories, and adjust discussion policies
- Assign moderator privileges and control user registrations
- Review overall system health and handle escalated moderation cases

## 5. Business Rules & Moderation
- Content violating community guidelines (spam, hate speech, etc.) is subject to removal and user sanctioning
- Member actions are logged for accountability
- Moderators must act transparently and cannot moderate their own content
- Automated checks for abuse or coordinated harmful activity support moderator workflows

## 6. Architecture Overview
The system is designed for security, scalability, and easy maintenance. Core components include:
- **User Management**: Authentication, authorization, and role control
- **Content Engine**: Handles creation, retrieval, and moderation of posts/comments
- **Reporting & Moderation Module**: Facilitates workflow for handling inappropriate content
- **Notification Service**: Powers real-time and asynchronous user alerts
- **Search & Indexing**: Enables content discovery through search and filters

---

# Discussion Board Business Rules & Moderation

## Overview
The Discussion Board aims to provide a vibrant, respectful space for exchanging ideas on political and economic topics. Strict business rules and robust moderation policies are essential to foster open, civil, and meaningful discussions. This document describes the rules, content policies, moderation roles, escalation processes, dispute resolution, and reporting mechanisms. It ensures transparent expectations for all users and supports platform success through user trust and community health.

## 1. Participation Rules
- Only registered and authenticated users may participate.
- Users must adhere to all terms of service and community guidelines.
- Posts and comments should stay on-topic (political or economic subjects) and contribute constructively to ongoing discussions.
- Harassment, hate speech, discrimination, or personal attacks are strictly forbidden.
- Spam, off-topic advertising, and solicitation are not permitted.
- Users must respect privacy and never post personal information.

## 2. Content Submission Policies
- Members may create, edit, or delete their own posts and comments.
- All content must remain factual, source-referenced where possible, and free from copyright infringement.
- The use of inappropriate language or graphic content is prohibited.
- Duplicated content and misleading titles are subject to removal.
- Users are responsible for all content published under their account.

## 3. Moderation Workflow
- Moderators and administrators have the authority to monitor all user-generated content.
- Flagged or reported posts and comments are reviewed within 24 hours.
- Moderators may edit, hide, or remove content that violates rules, providing clear reasons for their actions.
- Repeat or severe offenses can lead to temporary or permanent suspensions.
- All disciplinary actions are logged for accountability.

## 4. Reporting Mechanisms
- Any user can report posts or comments suspected of violating the rules.
- Reports are submitted via a designated form and logged with timestamps.
- Users may provide evidence or reasoning within the report.
- Moderators notify reporters of the outcome after review.

## 5. Escalation and Dispute Resolution
- Users can appeal moderation decisions through a formal appeals process.
- Appeals are reviewed by a panel of moderators and at least one administrator.
- Decisions on appeals are communicated in writing within five business days.
- Unresolved disputes may be escalated to the highest platform authority for a final decision.

## 6. Role-Specific Responsibilities
### Member
- Create, comment on, and engage with posts.
- Report inappropriate content.
- Follow platform rules at all times.

### Moderator
- Monitor content and enforce rules in all public contexts.
- Manage reported posts, execute disciplinary actions, and document outcomes.
- Engage with users to clarify policies and resolve minor conflicts.

### Admin
- Oversee moderation processes and make final decisions on escalations.
- Maintain community guidelines, set new policies, and manage high-level user privileges.
- Provide ongoing training for moderators to maintain consistent standards.

## 7. Rule Revision and Transparency
- All business rules and moderation policies are subject to regular review.
- Changes are communicated in advance, with rationale and opportunities for community feedback.
- Policy updates are documented for transparency.

## 8. Acceptance Criteria
- Users receive prompt feedback and rationale for moderation actions.
- Reports are handled efficiently and impartially.
- The moderation system supports a positive, open, and safe discussion environment.
- All roles understand and execute their responsibilities clearly.

## 9. Compliance & Monitoring
- Periodic audits ensure moderator compliance with policies.
- Metrics such as report resolution time and user satisfaction are tracked to guide improvements.
- Repeated failure to comply with rules at any level may lead to retraining or loss of privileges.

The above policies ensure a sustainable, trusted platform for all users while allowing for robust, meaningful debate within a supportive framework.

# 05_DiscussionBoard_Service_Overview_and_Architecture

## 1. Overview
This document outlines the high-level service architecture and core workflows for the Discussion Board, supporting political and economic topic discussions. The architecture is designed to deliver a scalable, user-centric platform that ensures engaging, civil discourse with clearly defined roles such as member, moderator, and admin. This overview avoids technical implementation details, instead focusing on business processes, role interactions, and key integration points.

## 2. Service Architecture
### 2.1 Component Map
- **User Portal:** Unified entry point providing responsive access for all user roles.
- **Authentication & Access Control:** Manages login, registration, and user role validation (member, moderator, admin), ensuring appropriate access levels per user.
- **Discussion Engine:** Core component handling post creation, comments, threads, reactions (like/dislike), and real-time updates.
- **Moderation Hub:** Interface and backend logic for moderator and admin actions — content review, reporting, user management, and dispute resolution.
- **Notification Service:** Provides system alerts for replies, mentions, moderation actions, and announcements.
- **Analytics & Reporting:** Aggregates usage metrics, sentiment trends, and moderation statistics for admins.

### 2.2 Role-Based Interaction Flow
Each role's interaction is governed by robust access policies. 
- **Members:** Create/view posts, comment, react, and engage with reporting.
- **Moderators:** Review and moderate content, manage flagged items, resolve conflicts.
- **Admins:** Configure system-level settings, manage users/roles, oversee policy compliance.

## 3. Workflow Summary
```
flowchart TD
    Login[User Login/Register] --> Home[Main Board View]
    Home -->|Create Post| NewPost[Post Creation]
    Home -->|Read Posts| PostDetail[Post Detail & Comments]
    PostDetail -->|Comment| CommentFlow[Comment Submission]
    PostDetail -->|React| ReactionFlow[Like/Dislike]
    PostDetail -->|Report| ReportFlow[Content Reporting]
    ReportFlow --> ModReview[Moderator Review]
    ModReview -->|Escalate| AdminReview[Admin Action]
    Home -->|Notifications| Notify[Check Alerts]
    AdminReview --> Decision[Resolution/Action]
```

## 4. Integration Points
- **Authentication Service:** Ensures secure, role-based access throughout all interactions.
- **Notification Module:** Integrates with user actions and moderation to keep all participants informed in real-time.
- **Moderation/Reporting:** Tight coupling between user reports, moderator actions, and system analytics for transparency.
- **Analytics export:** Aggregates data for business review and optimization.

## 5. Non-Functional Considerations
- **Scalability:** Designed to support active, large-scale discussions with responsive performance across devices.
- **Security & Privacy:** Implements strict access controls, content moderation, and user privacy safeguards.
- **Auditability:** All critical actions (moderation, admin changes, policy edits) are logged for compliance review.

## 6. High-Level Architectural Diagram
```
flowchart LR
    User[User Portal]
    Auth[Auth & Access Control]
    Discussion[Discussion Engine]
    ModHub[Moderation Hub]
    Notify[Notification Service]
    Analytics[Analytics & Reporting]

    User --> Auth
    Auth --> Discussion
    Discussion --> Notify
    Discussion --> ModHub
    ModHub --> Analytics
    Auth --> Admin[Admin Tools]
    Admin --> Analytics
```

---

For details regarding user role definitions, workflows, and business policies, refer to the corresponding documents in this series.

models.name: discussionboard_channels
models.description:
Discussion Board Channel entity - Implements the systematic domain requirement for logical grouping of sections or boards. This enables business-level partitioning of the discussion board infrastructure, supporting operations across multiple venues. Maintains full 3NF compliance by storing channel-level configuration only. For example, channels can represent separate geographic communities or topic groups under the same parent platform.

Key relationships: referenced by discussionboard_sections as a foreign key (one-to-many channel to section).
Special behaviors: Each channel is an atomic entity; no pre-aggregated statistics or derived values stored here.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each channel instance across the platform.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Channel name - Implements the labeling requirement for platform navigation. Business meaning: user-facing text for channel selection. Ensures normalization by storing only the atomic value here. For example, 'World Politics'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Channel description - Implements metadata requirement for administrative clarity and user context. Business meaning: long-form description visible in UI/tooltips. Remains atomic and optional for normalization. For example, 'A channel for global political news discussions.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the channel was created. Implements auditability and ordering requirement. Maintains normalized timestamp logging for business analytics (no derived statistics here).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for last modification of this channel entity. Fulfills the need for tracking administrative actions or platform reorganizations. No pre-aggregation, strictly the atomic event timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp for the channel. Implements the business rule for reversibility and audit trail. Null unless the channel is currently removed from active view. Maintains normalization and does not imply any historical statistics.

models.name: discussionboard_sections
models.description:
Discussion Board Section entity - Direct implementation of the systematic need for subdividing channels into manageable areas (e.g., boards, topics, or subgroups). This supports business logic for content structuring and access segmentation. Maintains strict 3NF compliance: each section is a minimal unit tied to a single channel, and no aggregation is stored.

For example, 'Economy' may be a section in 'World Politics' channel.

Key relationships: Each section references one channel by foreign key; sections are referenced by boards (content domain).
Special behaviors: Deletion marks are atomic; structural relationships only, not usage statistics.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each section within the discussion board, globally unique across all channels.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_channel_id
foreignFields.description: Parent channel's {@link discussionboard_channels.id}. Implements hierarchical structure and business partitioning for navigation and permissioning.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Section name - Implements the requirement for user navigation within a channel. Business meaning: short, user-facing label for the section. For example, 'Economy'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Section description - Provides context and detail about the section's focus for administrators and users. Maintains normalization by being atomic and non-derived; e.g., 'Discussion of global and national economies.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Atomic timestamp for section creation, used for ordering and audit logs. Ensures normalized structure for system-level tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for the most recent section update. Needed for administrative clarity and tracking structural changes over time. Remains atomic.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: If non-null, marks the section as soft deleted for potential recovery and audit trail. Implements reversibility without loss of history, compliant with normalized design.

models.name: discussionboard_configurations
models.description:
Discussion Board Configuration entity - This realizes the requirement for platform-wide or environment-specific system settings. It supports business ability to dynamically adjust service parameters without code changes. The model stores key-value configuration pairs with strict normalization (one row per config parameter).

For example: 'max_post_length', 'spam_detection_threshold', etc.

Key relationships: not directly referenced by other tables, but configurations are queried across the system for runtime behavior.
Special behaviors: Keys MUST be unique; only atomic values per row.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each configuration parameter row. Allows for audit, rollback, and historical tracking if paired with snapshots.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Configuration key name. Implements requirement for system parameterization. Atomic: e.g., 'max_post_length'.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Configuration value. Business meaning: stores the override for the specified key. Fully atomic; no denormalized/pre-computed data allowed (no parsing or aggregation).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description or purpose of this configuration parameter, for documentation. Ensures clarity for administrators. Optional, remains atomic and normalized.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of parameter creation. Supports requirement for modification audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent modification. Enables accurate tracking and rollback if required. Fully atomic event log.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: If filled, records parameter soft deletion timestamp. Maintains 3NF by never coalescing business meaning or usage data here.

models.name: discussionboard_notification_settings
models.description:
Discussion Board Notification Setting - Implements the business requirement for system-wide notification preferences and thresholds. This enables customization of notification behaviors used in business logic or for admin overrides. Each record represents a single atomic setting, ensuring full normalization.

Examples: 'default_email_frequency', 'alert_on_moderator_action', stored as key/value pairs.

Key relationships: Not a direct foreign key in this file, but referenced by notification domain logic.
Special behaviors: Key must be unique for lookups; model supports full auditability and system-level overrides.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each notification setting configuration row.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Setting key - Implements logical name for the notification configuration; fully atomic. For example, 'default_email_frequency'.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Setting value - Implements the actual configuration for this notification aspect. e.g., 'daily', 'immediate'. Atomic; usage is determined by business/application logic.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional field describing the meaning or effect of this notification setting. Supports administrative clarity; never pre-aggregated or derived. For example, 'If set to immediate, users will be notified instantly.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of setting creation. Required for audit trail and ordering. Remains fully normalized; no aggregation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of latest update for this setting. Maintains full auditability and supports change tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: If non-null, marks this setting as soft deleted; ensures reversibility and audit trail for deleted system settings. Atomic value for system auditing only.

models.name: discussionboard_members
models.description:
Discussion board member entity - Implements user registration and participation requirement from the requirements analysis. 

Represents individual users who can create posts, comments, and react to content. Each member record maintains normalized schema structure (3NF), holding atomic user-related attributes. For example, used whenever a user needs to establish an account and participate in discussion threads. 

Key relationships: foundational entity referenced by many business tables (posts, comments, reactions, reports).
Special behaviors: Registration, authentication, role assignment. No calculated/denormalized fields.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each member record.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Unique username for the member - Implements unique account creation requirement. Business meaning: Allows identification in the forum; must be unique. Ensures normalization as a single atomic property per user. For example, 'econ_debater42'. Username uniqueness must be enforced.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address for registration and notifications - Required by membership and password recovery requirements. Normalized, atomic, unique per user. For example, 'user@example.com'.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Display name, shown in posts/comments - Usability requirement. Allows custom presentation distinct from username. For example, 'Alice Lee'.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Password hash for secure authentication - Implements authentication and security requirements. Raw passwords are not stored; this field holds only hashes. For example, an Argon2 hash string.

plainFields.name: registered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member registered - For audit and participation log as required. Maintains normalization; atomic timestamp. For example, '2024-07-21T17:20:00Z'.

plainFields.name: last_login_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last member login - Used for user activity tracking and engagement analysis requirements. For example, updated each successful login.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the member account is active - Implements suspension/ban logic per rules. True means active, false means suspended/banned.

models.name: discussionboard_moderators
models.description:
Discussion board moderator entity - Implements the moderation staffing and role elevation requirement.

Represents users elevated to the moderator role, responsible for review, editing, and policy enforcement. Maintains 3NF by only referencing the member and managing moderator-specific assignment logic. For example, used whenever a member is promoted to moderator, and can be demoted later. 

Key relationships: Each moderator references a member; links to admin who promoted.
Special behaviors: Only one moderator per member at any given time; moderator role can be revoked/assigned.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each moderator assignment record.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Moderated user's {@link discussionboard_members.id} - Identifies which member is assigned moderator role. Required linkage for role elevation.

foreignFields.name: promoted_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin user {@link discussionboard_admins.id} who elevated this member - Captures the administrative actor for audit and compliance purposes.

plainFields.name: assigned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when moderator role was granted - Audit of elevation process. Enforces event logs required for compliance.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when moderator role was revoked, if ever - Required for demotion and historical tracking. Null if still active moderator.

models.name: discussionboard_admins
models.description:
Discussion board administrator entity - Implements admin management and system policy configuration requirements from the analysis.

Represents users who hold administrator powers, capable of configuring the board, promoting/demoting roles, and handling escalated moderation. Admins are a subset of members. Maintains normalization by referencing the member record and managing admin-specific appointments/terminations. For example, new admins are appointed by existing admins, with record of appointment action.

Key relationships: Always linked to a member; may reference appointing admin (for audit).
Special behaviors: Enforces business rule that admin powers are explicitly appointed and tracked; admin role demotion is supported.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each admin record.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Admin user's {@link discussionboard_members.id} - Always references a member (never null); an admin is a member.

foreignFields.name: appointed_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: The {@link discussionboard_admins.id} of the admin that performed this appointment - Maintains audit trail and compliance; can be null for the system's initial admin.

plainFields.name: appointed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin role was granted - Required for compliance with audit and transparency rules.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin role was revoked - Null if still admin. Required for demotion and role delegation history.

models.name: discussionboard_role_change_logs
models.description:
Logs of all role changes (member to moderator/admin, moderator/admin demotion) - Implements full auditability, transparency, and traceability of role elevation/demotion per compliance and security requirements in the analysis.

Each log records the before/after role, actor initiating the change, and the affected user. Maintains normalization (3NF) by referencing affected member, actor, and clearly separating each event. For example, used for post-hoc reviews, policy enforcement, and compliance audits.

Key relationships: Affected member, acting admin, relevant old/new moderator/admin ids.
Special behaviors: Immutable event log, not editable. Serves as source of truth for role change history.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each role change event.

foreignFields.name: affected_member_id
foreignFields.description: The affected {@link discussionboard_members.id} whose role changed. Required for all events.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_id
foreignFields.description: The admin {@link discussionboard_admins.id} who performed the role change - Required for compliance traceability.

foreignFields.name: from_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator record {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} representing role before change (null if not previously a moderator).

foreignFields.name: to_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator record {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} representing role after change (null if not becoming a moderator).

foreignFields.name: from_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin record {@link discussionboard_admins.id} representing role before change (null if not previously admin).

foreignFields.name: to_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin record {@link discussionboard_admins.id} representing role after change (null if not becoming admin).

plainFields.name: change_type
plainFields.description: Type of role change - Implements policy audit requirement. Examples: 'promote_to_moderator', 'demote_from_admin', 'promote_to_admin'.

plainFields.name: change_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation or reason for the role change - Satisfies policy transparency and compliance requirements. Allows admins to document specific context for audit/review.

plainFields.name: changed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the role change event - Fulfills audit trail requirement for accurate event ordering.

models.name: discussionboard_boards
models.description: Board entity - This implements the requirement to support topic-centric discussion spaces from the requirements document. Provides organizational structure for grouping posts by topic (e.g., Politics, Economics). Maintains 3NF compliance by storing board-specific details without content data. For example, a politics board holds all political discussions and posts. Key relationships: references by posts. Special behaviors: board names must be unique within the system.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Board display name - Implements requirement for clear topic identification. Human-readable title, e.g., 'Current Affairs'. Ensures normalization by holding only atomic data. Cannot be null.

plainFields.name: slug
plainFields.description: Unique board identifier - Implements friendly URLs and quick access per board. Used to generate access links, e.g., 'politics'. Kept normalized as a unique value. Cannot be null.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Board description - Implements need for user guidance about content focus. Describes what topics/posts are expected, e.g., 'Debate ongoing political and economic affairs'. Normalizes board meta details. Nullable for minimal boards.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for board creation - Implements audit trail requirement. Captures when the board was added. Essential for record-keeping. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for board last update - Implements requirement for modification tracking. Required for operational auditing. Not nullable.

models.name: discussionboard_posts
models.description: Discussion post entity - Implements requirement for user-generated content, main feature for posting discussions. Encapsulates post content, author reference, board association, and metadata. Maintains 3NF compliance – all content and relations are atomic. For example, an economy discussion post with attached metadata, belonging to a specific board and member. Key relationships: belongs to a board and an author. Special behaviors: Supports edit and snapshot tracking in related models.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: board_id
foreignFields.description: Board reference - Maps post to its parent board {@link discussionboard_boards.id}. Ensures posts are organized and policed by board topic. Not nullable.

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: Post author reference - Refers to author's member id {@link discussionboard_members.id} from Actors. Required for traceability and policy enforcement. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Post headline - Implements clear topic identification from requirements. Atomic, concise summary for display. Normalized data. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main post content - Implements user contribution facility. Full markdown/text of the post. 3NF: Solely post-specific content. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: view_count
plainFields.description: Post view counter - Implements metric tracking without denormalization. Raw access counter only, recalculated in MV if aggregate needed. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: is_locked
plainFields.description: Thread lock flag - Implements moderation behavior. If true, prevents further edits/comments. Maintains normalized data. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - Implements audit trail. Enables temporal sorting and moderation. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp - Implements requirement for modification tracking and concurrency handling. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp - Implements need for recoverable deletion. Null means active, set when marked deleted. Nullable to maintain audit. 3NF compliant.

models.name: discussionboard_post_edits
models.description: Post edits log entity - Implements edit-tracking and audit history. Captures every change made to a post for moderator review/rollback. Fulfills snapshot and traceability requirements. Maintains 3NF by separating edits from base post. For example, a revision made by a user or moderator is logged here. Key relationships: references original post, editor, and edit metadata. No denormalized content. Used in moderation dispute resolution and rollback workflows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to original post {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Links edit history with its post. 3NF: No duplication of post content.

foreignFields.name: editor_id
foreignFields.description: Edit author reference {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Identifies user (or moderator) who made the change. 3NF by avoiding repeating editor details. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: edit_summary
plainFields.description: Short edit description - Implements moderator review requirements. Explains reason for change, e.g., 'Corrected typo'. 3NF compliant. Nullable if none given.

plainFields.name: body_after_edit
plainFields.description: Post content after edit - Implements snapshot auditability. Stores revised body for this edit, not pre-calculated or aggregated. For example, after typo correction. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Edit creation timestamp. Implements audit/compliance, enables edit ordering. Not nullable.

models.name: discussionboard_post_snapshots
models.description: Post snapshot entity - Implements versioned history and rollback for posts. Stores complete post state at key points (creation, major edits, moderator actions). 3NF by separating temporal states from base post. For example, preserving a pre-moderation version for audit review. Key relationships: references post and snapshot creator. Snapshots are referenced by moderation modules if applicable.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the post being snapshotted {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Required for mapping snapshot to content. Not nullable.

foreignFields.name: created_by_id
foreignFields.description: Snapshot creator reference {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Maintains normalized responsibility chain. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Snapshot of post's title at the time - Enables historical traceability per requirements. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Snapshot of content body - Preserves versioned information for audits and appeals. 3NF: no derived data.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when snapshot was generated - For audit trails and moderation.
Not nullable.

models.name: discussionboard_comments
models.description: Comment entity - Implements requirement for threaded responses to posts. Stores individual comments made by users on posts. Maintains 3NF as each comment is atomic and related to a specific post/thread. For example, a member replies to a post or another comment. Key relationships: links post, comment thread, and author. Special behavior: supports soft deletion and allows for moderation tracking via related modules.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent post {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Ensures comment is scoped to a post. Not nullable.

foreignFields.name: thread_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the comment thread (root or subthread) {@link discussionboard_comment_threads.id}. Enables nested/discussion threading per requirements. Not nullable.

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to member authoring comment {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Enables moderation and accountability. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Comment content - Implements threaded discussion and reply requirements. Atomic user-written text field. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: depth
plainFields.description: Nesting depth - Implements support for multi-level threading. Indicates level (0=root, 1=reply, etc). 3NF – purely comment-specific, no summary. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: is_edited
plainFields.description: Edit flag - Implements editing traceability requirements. True if comment was edited. Supports moderation and transparency. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Comment creation time - For ordering and audit trail. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modified time - For traceability and moderation. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete time - Implements recoverable deletion. Null if active, set on removal. Not nullable; maintains full audit history.

models.name: discussionboard_comment_threads
models.description: Comment thread entity - Implements the requirement for grouped/nested commenting. Tracks top-level and sub-threads to organize comment hierarchies under posts. Maintains 3NF by holding only threading and structure data, not comment content. For example, a root thread under a post and a reply thread under another comment. Key relationships: associated with a post and may reference a parent thread for nesting. Supports performance optimization and UI rendering for large discussions.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to post that the thread belongs to {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Each thread belongs to a single post. Not nullable.

foreignFields.name: parent_thread_id
foreignFields.description: Self-referential parent thread for nested comments (nullable) {@link discussionboard_comment_threads.id}. Supports multi-level threading. Nullable for root level.

plainFields.name: depth
plainFields.description: Thread depth - Implements threading visualization. 0=root, >0=nested thread. 3NF: atomic structural info only. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Thread creation timestamp - For audit trail, UI ordering. Not nullable.

models.name: discussionboard_comment_edits
models.description: Comment edits log entity - Implements edit-tracking and audit history for comments. Captures every change made to a comment for moderator review or potential rollback. Fulfills snapshot and traceability requirements. Maintains 3NF by separating edits from the base comment. For example, a revision made to fix a typo is logged here. Key relationships: references original comment, editor, and edit metadata. Used in moderation troubleshooting and rollback workflows. No denormalized content.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original comment {@link discussionboard_comments.id}. Links edit to its base comment. Maintains 3NF: no duplication of comment content or thread.

foreignFields.name: editor_id
foreignFields.description: Reference for editor of the comment (member or moderator) {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Ensures traceability. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: edit_summary
plainFields.description: Short summary explaining reason for edit - Implements requirement for moderator review. 3NF compliant. Nullable if not specified by user/editor.

plainFields.name: body_after_edit
plainFields.description: Comment contents after edit - Captures full content for audit and rollback. Not nullable; ensures traceability, versioning, and full history without denormalized data.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Edit creation timestamp. Implements edit order, audit trail, and moderation workflows.

models.name: discussionboard_post_reactions
models.description:
Discussion board post reactions - This model implements the requirement to enable users to express opinions (like/dislike) on posts, as documented in the business requirements (see Main Features: Voting, User Journeys: Member Participation). 

Business explanation: Records each user's reaction (like/dislike) to a specific post, enabling engagement tracking while preventing duplicate reactions per user per post. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating reaction data from post content and aggregations. For example, a user can 'like' a post, and this entry records their intent specifically for that post, without summary fields.

Key relationships: Links to the reacting member and the associated post. Special behaviors: Enforces one reaction per user per post through unique constraint, soft-deletes allow for undo/redo actions.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each post reaction.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Indicates which registered member made the reaction.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Associates the reaction with a particular post in the board.

plainFields.name: reaction_type
plainFields.description:
Type of reaction - Implements the voting/feedback requirement.

Business meaning: 'like', 'dislike', or future extension values (e.g. 'insightful'). Ensures normalization as all possible reactions are atomic per entry. For example, a member can express a 'like' or 'dislike' on a post, but never both simultaneously on the same post.

Constraint: Application layer restricts values (enum); index allows future extensibility. Required field.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reaction was first recorded. Ensures accurate historical auditing to support undo functionality, behavioral patterns, or retroactive analysis. For example, seeing how engagement peaks over time.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Soft-delete timestamp - Implements reversible actions.

If null: Reaction is active; if set: reaction is considered deleted (e.g., user "unlikes" a post). Ensures normalization by not physically removing entries and maintaining an audit trail. Example: Allows for undo/redo of likes/dislikes.

models.name: discussionboard_comment_reactions
models.description:
Discussion board comment reactions - This model implements the requirement for users to provide feedback (likes/dislikes) on individual comments in discussion threads (see Main Features, User Journeys, and Engagement KPIs). 

Business explanation: Captures each user reaction to a comment, allowing fine-grained participation and sentiment analysis at the comment level. Maintains 3NF compliance by storing each user-comment reaction atomically. For example, a user can 'like' or 'dislike' a comment in a thread and this entry logs that action with traceability and reversibility.

Key relationships: Links to both the reacting member and the specific comment. Special behaviors: Enforces one reaction per user per comment, supports soft delete for undo/redo, and enables future extensibility for reaction types.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each comment reaction entry.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Identifies which platform member submitted the reaction to a comment.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged comment's {@link discussionboard_comments.id}. Specifies the comment being reacted to.

plainFields.name: reaction_type
plainFields.description:
Type of reaction - Implements the core like/dislike feature for comments.

Business meaning: Allowed values are 'like', 'dislike' (future-proof to support more). Atomic, normalized representation for each user-comment interaction. Ensures a member can record only a single reaction per comment. For example: registers a 'like' to a comment, excluding duplications.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp at which the reaction was made. For accurate historical analysis, behavioral tracking, and compliance/auditing. Required field. For example, differentiates old vs new reactions.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp - Enables undo/redo for user feedback and preserves historical record, following audit trail requirements. Null means reaction is current; timestamp means it was removed/undone. Supports moderation and compliance.

models.name: discussionboard_reports
models.description:
Report Entity - This implements the reporting and moderation requirements for tracking content suspected of violating platform rules (see sections 4, 5, and 6 in the requirements analysis). 

Business explanation: Each record represents a distinct instance where a member reports a post or comment for review, enabling formal moderation and resolution workflows. Maintains 3NF by storing each report and its relationships, without embedding calculated or summary data. For example, when a member flags a post for hate speech, a discussionboard_reports entry is created.

Key relationships: references the reported content (post or comment), the reporting member, and the selected category. Also links to the report's resolution log for auditability.
Special behaviors: Only authenticated members can submit; moderators/admins append resolution status through logs. Subsequent action is auditable through the associated logs.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each report; satisfies normalization and distributed system compatibility.

foreignFields.name: reported_by_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reporting member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Foreign key pointing to the user that submitted the report.

foreignFields.name: report_category_id
foreignFields.description: Category's {@link discussionboard_report_categories.id}. Classifies the report according to the selected category (e.g., spam, harassment).

foreignFields.name: target_post_id
foreignFields.description: Target post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Set when the report concerns a post. Nullable to support comment targeting.

foreignFields.name: target_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Target comment's {@link discussionboard_comments.id}. Set when the report concerns a comment. Nullable to support post targeting.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: User-provided explanation for the report - Implements reporting detail requirements. Describes why the content was reported, supporting moderator decision-making. Example: 'This post contains personal attacks and inappropriate language.' Enforced as required for context clarity.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Business status of the report, such as 'open', 'in_review', 'resolved', 'rejected' - Implements moderation workflow requirement. Used by moderators to track processing state. Only normalized status labels allowed here (no summary/calculation). Example: 'in_review'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when report was created - Implements audit and traceability requirement. For example, helps measure report processing times.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: When the report was resolved - Implements resolution tracking requirement. Nullable for open/in-review reports. Example: when moderator completes review.

models.name: discussionboard_report_logs
models.description:
Report Log Entity - Implements audit and traceability requirements for the moderation process (requirements analysis section 3 and 5).

Business explanation: Records every status/action taken on a report (discussionboard_reports), providing a complete history for each case. Maintains 3NF by capturing atomic actions with actor, comment, and timestamp data; never stores pre-aggregated or summary fields. Used, for example, when a moderator changes a report's status or adds a resolution note.

Key relationships: Links to the underlying report and the acting moderator or admin. Enables full moderation workflow replay for compliance and accountability.
Special behaviors: Immutable (no edit/delete) after logging; supports audit trail for dispute handling.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier per log entry, required for reliable chaining and auditability.

foreignFields.name: report_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to {@link discussionboard_reports.id}. Indicates which report this log entry documents.

foreignFields.name: actor_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to {@link discussionboard_moderators.id}. Indicates which moderator or admin executed the log action.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Moderation action performed - Implements step tracking requirement (e.g., 'assigned', 'in_review', 'replied', 'resolved', 'rejected', etc.). Maintains normalization by recording only atomic event. For example: 'resolved'.

plainFields.name: action_comment
plainFields.description: Optional comment by moderator/admin for context - Supports requirement for context-rich logs. May explain why action taken or rationale behind moderation. Example: 'User confirmed violation; post removed.' Nullable; not present for all actions.

plainFields.name: timestamp
plainFields.description: Time when log entry was created - Fulfills sequential/log order tracking requirement. Used for reconstructing timeline and compliance checking.

models.name: discussionboard_report_categories
models.description:
Report Category Entity - Implements the requirement to normalize types and reasons for reporting (requirements analysis section 4 and moderation flows).

Business explanation: Defines allowed, controlled vocabulary for report classification (e.g., 'spam', 'abuse', 'off-topic'). Ensures that all user reports have a meaningful, actionable category, which helps in triaging and statistical tracking. Maintains 3NF by representing each category as an atomic entity. For example, a user reporting spam selects the corresponding category_id.

Key relationships: Used as foreign key by discussionboard_reports for category normalization.
Special behaviors: Only Admin can add/edit/delete categories to prevent inconsistency.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier per category to support reliable referencing.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique category name - Implements controlled vocabulary for valid report types. Example: 'spam'. Enforced unique for referential clarity.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Category description - Explains category purpose to end-users/moderators. For example: 'Reports regarding unsolicited advertisements.' Required for clarity.

models.name: discussionboard_moderation_actions
models.description:
Moderation Action Log - This implements the 'Moderation Workflow' and 'Role-Specific Responsibilities' requirements, capturing every moderator/admin action taken on user-generated content. 

Business explanation: Stores a normalized, chronological log of all action events related to moderation (such as warning users, deleting posts, editing content, suspending accounts), ensuring accountability and traceability for dispute resolution and audits. Maintains 3NF by referencing related entities with foreign keys (not duplicating content or user-info). For example, useful for reconstructing a moderation timeline.

Key relationships: links to moderators/admins (actor), affected content (post/comment via foreign keys), and creates a record for appeals. Special behaviors: Immutable record—entries should never be deleted or altered after creation, only appended.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each moderation action log entry.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator actor responsible for the moderation action - references the moderator who performed the action via {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} in Actors domain. Ensures role accountability. Nullable to allow actions performed by admins directly.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin actor responsible for the moderation action - references the admin who performed the action via {@link discussionboard_admins.id} in Actors domain. Ensures role accountability. Nullable to allow actions performed by moderators directly.

foreignFields.name: target_post_id
foreignFields.description: Targeted post (if applicable) - references {@link discussionboard_posts.id} in Content domain. Nullable for actions not tied to a post (e.g., user warnings).

foreignFields.name: target_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Targeted comment (if applicable) - references {@link discussionboard_comments.id} in Content domain. Nullable for actions not tied to a comment.

foreignFields.name: affected_member_id
foreignFields.description: Affected member - references {@link discussionboard_members.id}. The user who is the subject of the moderation action.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action. Implements business logic around moderation event categorization (e.g., 'edit', 'delete', 'warn', 'suspend', 'reinstate'). Enables filtering and analytics. For example, supports reporting on frequency of warning vs deletion events.

plainFields.name: action_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation or reason for the moderation action. Implements requirement for documentation and transparency. Ensures normalization by separating event log from business rule/policy text. For example: 'Hate speech per Content Policy 2.3'.

plainFields.name: action_note
plainFields.description: Supplementary context or moderator note. Supports nuanced explanations for audits/disputes, and ensures normalization by storing annotations distinctly from main content. Example: 'Repeat offense after prior warning.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was recorded. Enables audit trails and time-based analyses. Enforces normalization by consistently storing event times in this domain table. Required and never null.

models.name: discussionboard_moderation_appeals
models.description:
Moderation Appeals - Implements requirements from 'Escalation and Dispute Resolution' and 'Role-Specific Responsibilities', enabling members to appeal moderation outcomes. 

Business explanation: This table normalizes appeal submissions, allowing affected members to formally contest moderation actions. Maintains normalization by separating appeals from moderation logs and allowing multiple appeals per action if appropriate. For example, supports future analytics around appeal rates and outcomes.

Key relationships: links each appeal to a specific member (the appellant), the related moderation action, and creates the basis for related decisions. Special behaviors: Each appeal's status and progress is tracked, but business logic prevents duplicate active appeals for the same moderation action by the same member.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique ID for each moderation appeal.

foreignFields.name: moderation_action_id
foreignFields.description: The moderation action being appealed. References {@link discussionboard_moderation_actions.id}; implements requirement that appeals always correspond to a concrete moderation event.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Appellant member - references {@link discussionboard_members.id} (in Actors domain) of the user submitting the appeal.

plainFields.name: appeal_reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by the member for appeal. Ensures normalization by storing structured user input distinct from system logs. For example: 'Content removed in error, did not violate guideline.'

plainFields.name: appeal_status
plainFields.description: Current status of the appeal (e.g., 'pending', 'under_review', 'decided', 'withdrawn'). Supports business processes around escalation and supports queries on appeal state. Implemented as normalized string, not computed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the appeal was submitted. Required for time-based analytics and retention policies.

plainFields.name: last_updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to the appeal record (e.g., status change). Ensures proper lifecycle tracking.

models.name: discussionboard_appeal_decisions
models.description:
Appeal Decisions - Implements the 'Appeals Process', 'Escalation and Dispute Resolution', and admin decision reporting requirements.

Business explanation: Captures individual decisions made during appeal review by moderators/admins. Normalizes how each decision on an appeal is recorded, who made it, and the rationale. Maintains normalization by separating decision data from appeals, supporting multi-stage review or panel votes. For example: can store decision history, rationales, and timestamps for compliance and analytics.

Key relationships: references specific appeals, identifies the admin/moderator who decided, and links to the Actors domain. Special behaviors: Once created, decisions are immutable, supporting audit trails.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each appeal decision.

foreignFields.name: appeal_id
foreignFields.description: References the specific appeal under review, via {@link discussionboard_moderation_appeals.id}. Implements requirement that decisions are always tied to a submitted appeal.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator making the appeal decision. References {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} for audit compliance. Nullable if the decision was made by an admin.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin making the appeal decision. References {@link discussionboard_admins.id} for audit compliance. Nullable if the decision was made by a moderator.

plainFields.name: decision_outcome
plainFields.description: Outcome of the appeal review (e.g., 'upheld', 'overturned', 'modified', 'escalated'). Implements normalized, auditable record of resolution.

plainFields.name: decision_rationale
plainFields.description: Explanation of the decision (business/policy rationale). Ensures normalization by keeping detailed reasoning separate from logs. Example: 'Post restored; guideline not violated.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when the decision was finalized. Required for audit trails and analytics.

models.name: discussionboard_notifications
models.description:
Discussion Board Notification Entity - This model implements the delivery and audit requirement for all real-time and asynchronous notifications in the discussion board system, as specified in the requirements analysis for user feedback, moderation alerts, and system messages.

Business explanation: Each notification represents a single event delivered to a user (member, moderator, or admin) such as a mention, reply, moderation action, report escalation, or system notice. This design ensures proper 3NF compliance by storing atomic, individual notification records per user. For example, when a member is mentioned in a comment, a notification entry is created and delivered only to them.

Key relationships: Tied by foreign keys to members/actors table and content (post, comment, report, etc.). Allows targeting any user for any board event.
Special behaviors: Stores type, target, delivery/read status, and timestamps. Supports reliable delivery, tracking, and audit for compliance.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each notification record for audit and delivery tracking.

foreignFields.name: recipient_member_id
foreignFields.description: Target recipient's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Links each notification to the intended user, who may be a member, moderator, or admin.

foreignFields.name: trigger_actor_id
foreignFields.description: The user {@link discussionboard_members.id}, moderator, or admin who performed the action that generated this notification.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Type of notification (e.g., mention, reply, like, report, moderation_alert, system_announcement) - Implements requirement for tracking notification category and triggering appropriate UI rendering. Ensures normalization by storing type as an atomic string. Example: 'mention', 'report', 'system_announcement'.

plainFields.name: target_post_id
plainFields.description: If this notification is about a post, the target post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Null if N/A. Implements event referencing for modular notification design.

plainFields.name: target_comment_id
plainFields.description: If about a comment, the target comment's {@link discussionboard_comments.id}. Null if N/A.

plainFields.name: target_report_id
plainFields.description: If about a report, the relevant report's {@link discussionboard_reports.id}. Null if N/A.

plainFields.name: target_section_id
plainFields.description: If about a section or board, references {@link discussionboard_sections.id}. Null if not applicable.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Delivery timestamp for when notification was actually pushed to the user (email, web, etc.). Implements audit requirement for event delivery logs.

plainFields.name: read_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user viewed this notification. Null until read by recipient. Allows audit and unread count functionality.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the notification entry was created in the DB. Required for audit trail and sorting.

models.name: discussionboard_notification_preferences
models.description:
Discussion Board Notification Preferences - Implements the user-configurable notification preference requirement for the discussion board system, allowing each member to choose which types or channels of notifications they wish to receive.

Business explanation: Each record links a member with their individual notification settings (e.g., email, push, web), supporting requirements for user personalization and compliance with communication opt-out regulations. Maintains proper 3NF by splitting member-to-preference mappings and avoids redundancy (no preferences stored on the member object itself).

Example: A user may silence 'system_announcement' notices but permit 'reply' and 'mention' notifications. Key relationships: belongs to one member, can be extended for per-channel preferences.
Special behaviors: Unique index per member, atomic on/off flags per notification type. Supports UI rendering for notification settings per member.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique per distinct preferences instance to support audit trails and changes.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Owner user's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Each preferences record belongs to one member.

plainFields.name: enable_email
plainFields.description: Whether to send notifications via email. Implements the multi-channel notification setting requirement (opt-in/out).

plainFields.name: enable_web_push
plainFields.description: Whether to send notifications via browser push. Example: Member disables all web push notifications but accepts email.

plainFields.name: enable_system_announcements
plainFields.description: If set, member will also get system-level announcements (policy changes, upgrades). Implements granular opt-in/out rule from requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of preference entry creation. Enables audit and UI display of preference change recency.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last time any part of these preferences were changed. Allows compliance tracking per member.

models.name: discussionboard_content_policies
models.description:
Content Policy Model - This implements the 'policy definition & update tracking' requirement from the documented business rules and moderation policies. 

Business purpose: Governs community guidelines and permissible content on the board, defining what is and isn't allowed. Maintains 3NF by strictly separating policy meta from rule text, and associating with change logs for audit. For example, an admin can update this table to change offensive language filtering rules.

Key relationships: Referenced by logs, may be tied to moderation actions (defined in other domains).
Special behaviors: Effective/expiration tracking, scope of applicability, and active/withdrawn status.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each content policy.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Policy code - Implements the identification aspect of content policies for referencing in reports and logs. Business meaning: Unique short string (e.g., 'GENERAL', 'SPAM', 'HATE_SPEECH', etc.) that identifies this policy across the system. Ensures normalization by not reiterating policy meaning elsewhere; logs or moderation reference this code instead. For example, a moderator's action references 'SPAM' if acting under the anti-spam policy.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Human-readable title of the policy - Implements requirement of clear policy communication. Business meaning: User-facing summary of the policy (e.g., 'No Hate Speech', 'No Spam'). Ensures normalization by preventing repetition in related tables. For example, visible to members on the board's policy page.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed policy text - Implements detailed requirement explanation from policy docs. Business meaning: The full text or markdown of the policy (rules, examples, etc). Ensures normalization by avoiding duplication in logs. For example, can be displayed as the guideline text in the board UI.

plainFields.name: effective_from
plainFields.description: Policy effective start timestamp - Implements versioning/audit need for knowing when this policy takes effect. Business meaning: From this datetime, the policy is in force. Ensures normalization by separating temporal aspects from identifiers/text. For example, new hate speech wording might be effective May 1, 2025.

plainFields.name: effective_to
plainFields.description: Policy expiration/withdrawal timestamp - Implements requirement of temporal scoping. Business meaning: Until this datetime, the policy applies; null if still current. Ensures normalization—time scoping is managed in a single place. For example, an old policy that's replaced will have this set.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether the policy is currently active - Implements enforcement logic. Business meaning: Admins can deactivate a policy for maintenance/retirement. Ensures normalization—removes special status flags from related tables. For example, inactive policies are hidden from UI and not enforced.

models.name: discussionboard_business_rules
models.description:
Business Rule Model - Implements the 'business rules, moderation logic, and platform-wide process configuration' requirements. 

Business purpose: Stores board-wide operational rules (such as edit/delete restrictions, notification toggles, content length maximums, etc). Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic rule properties, distinct from content policy details and change logs. For example, changing the maximum allowed post length updates this table.

Key relationships: May be referenced from moderation or configuration logs (other domains).
Special behaviors: Supports toggling, parameterizing, and enumerating global rule options (e.g., max edits, grace period mins).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each business rule.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Rule key - Implements structured reference and lookup for business rules system-wide. Business meaning: Unique identifier such as 'MAX_POST_LENGTH', 'ALLOW_POST_EDITING', etc. Ensures normalization by preventing duplication in logs or configs. For example: referenced programmatically or displayed in admin settings.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Rule value - Implements requirement to parameterize settings. Business meaning: Value as string (can be int, bool, etc, encoded as string) for flexible config. Ensures normalization by centralizing config values. For example: '10000' for MAX_POST_LENGTH, 'true' for ALLOW_POST_EDITING.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Rule human description - Implements requirement of explainability for business rules. Business meaning: User/admin-facing explanation of this rule and how it's applied. Ensures normalization by separating explanation from the rule key/value. For example: 'Maximum characters a post can have.'

models.name: discussionboard_policy_change_logs
models.description:
Policy Change Log Model - Implements audit/compliance and traceability requirements from policy governance documentation. 

Business purpose: Records every change (add/modify/deactivate) to content policies or business rules, supporting rollback, accountability, and regulation compliance. Maintains 3NF by splitting log records from the entities being changed and snapshotting pre/post values. For example, when an admin updates a policy description, a record is inserted here.

Key relationships: Optionally references the changed policy or rule.
Special behaviors: Retains both the actor (admin) and before/after values for compliance audits.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each change log entry.

foreignFields.name: changed_policy_id
foreignFields.description: If non-null, links to the affected Content Policy's {@link discussionboard_content_policies.id}. For logging which policy was changed.

foreignFields.name: changed_rule_id
foreignFields.description: If non-null, links to the affected Business Rule's {@link discussionboard_business_rules.id}. For logging which rule was changed.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin actor performing the change - Links to the {@link discussionboard_admins.id} in Actors domain for compliance logging.

plainFields.name: change_type
plainFields.description: Type of change - Implements requirement to distinguish operations ('add', 'edit', 'deactivate', etc). Business meaning: Describes the action (enum-like); e.g., 'ADD', 'EDIT', 'DEACTIVATE'. Ensures normalization as a single column, referenced in reports, etc. For example: shown in the admin change history UI.

plainFields.name: before_value
plainFields.description: Pre-change JSON value - Implements audit requirement of historical state. Business meaning: JSON-encoded string of content policy or rule before the change. Ensures normalization by snapshotting original value rather than duplicating all properties. For example, for edits, this holds the old version of the policy/rule.

plainFields.name: after_value
plainFields.description: Post-change JSON value - Implements audit requirement for traceability. Business meaning: JSON-encoded string of policy/rule after the change. Ensures normalization via atomic recording. For example: allows rollback if needed; basis for audit comparison.

plainFields.name: changed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of change - Implements chronology/auditing requirement. Business meaning: When the change was made. Ensures strict temporal audit log. For example, supports timelines of admin actions.
